patches.value: L(K) is the scalar extension to K of the free rank-three Chevalley Z-Lie algebra on formal basis ξ,η,ζ, with brackets [ζ,ξ]=2ξ, [ζ,η]=-2η, [ξ,η]=ζ, extended bilinearly and antisymmetrically with zero self-brackets. This is (Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K in the original notation, with ξ,η,ζ labeled there by x,y,h. These are abstract Chevalley generators, not their possibly nonfaithful operator images on V. The generators ξ⊗1,η⊗1,ζ⊗1 act on V(K) by the operators x,y,h induced from M. This is the Chevalley construction also in characteristic 2.

patches.new: F001 gives spanning of M_R by (b e_i), and N001 gives their R-independence: a relation divided by the nonzero complex scalar b is a relation on e. Hence they form an R-basis. The same proof applies to every nonzero scalar that generates J over R, since it uses only that scalar's nonzeroness and its generating property.
